questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped question explicitly contrasts systematic and random errors for wire-diameter measurements.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Describe one effect of each error type in an apparatus context.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Identify consistent offset versus reading-to-reading variation.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Treating all variation as the same kind of error.

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped part asks for a systematic-error example with an analogue voltmeter.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Connect an instrument fault to a consistent directional effect.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: State an apparatus cause and explain its repeated offset.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Giving a random viewing variation as a systematic fault.

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped paired part asks for a random-error example using the same instrument.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Identify a cause that can move readings in either direction.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Calling a fixed calibration shift random error.

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped timing context shows several physical and human sources of discrepancy.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Suggest credible measurement causes without applying later uncertainty methods.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Separate the intended measured event from timing and sound-detection limitations.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Assuming a stopwatch reading must equal the ideal motion time.

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped part asks how random errors are reduced while using the selected instrument.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Choose repetition, varied positions and averaging appropriately.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Take multiple independent readings, then calculate a mean.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Repeating one identical recorded value rather than remeasuring.
